reviewed_by: Claude review of the phone sidebar drawer stacking fix
reason: On phones (<=760px) in the standard themes (Dark verified; Light uses the same rules), the open sidebar drawer (z-index 10) and its scrim (8) sat under full-width resource inspectors (16), so the drawer was hidden and scrim taps hit the inspector form. Zero already layers its open drawer at 80/75 and was verified unaffected. The standard open drawer and scrim now use the same 80/75, scoped to .app-shell:not(.sidebar-collapsed) inside the 760px query. Selected: the phone-shell entries on mobile-chromium and mobile-webkit, which include the new regression 'phone shell opens the sidebar drawer above resource inspectors' (findings, assets, evidence, sources and library inspectors in Zero Dark and Dark: drawer and scrim are the hit targets, a scrim tap closes the drawer and leaves the inspector route intact, drawer navigation works over an inspector) plus the existing phone shell journeys that open the drawer.
exclusions: No full suites. No Python, native or frontend unit changes: the fix is CSS-only and its behavior is observable only in a browser. Desktop and compact projects are excluded because the CSS sits inside the 760px media query. No screenshot baselines change: every baseline is captured with the sidebar collapsed or in Zero, whose unlayered rules already set 80/75. The new test also passed locally on narrow and on the small and wide phone projects.
